article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Morning Brief
article.dek: All three Thanksgiving games came down to the final seconds, the board held its three Sunday cards overnight, and Denver plays Pittsburgh today in the rain.

items.headline: Eagles 39, Cowboys 38 — Philly erases a 21-point hole in Dallas
paragraphs: The Eagles trailed 31-10 in the third quarter and won it anyway. Joe Milton, starting with Jalen Hurts out, threw for 331 yards and accounted for four touchdowns against his old team. Jake Elliott drilled a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left.

Dallas led 28-10 at halftime and 31-10 after three quarters. Dak Prescott threw for 265 yards and two touchdowns, and Javonte Williams had three total touchdowns. It was not enough. A blocked punt and a big kickoff return in the fourth quarter swung it.
The Eagles are 4-7 now. The Cowboys fall to 5-7. All three Thanksgiving games were decided in the final seconds.
items.takeaway: Three Thanksgiving games, three finishes at the gun. Nothing to bet after the fact — the Sunday cards are where the action is now.

items.headline: Bills 13, Chiefs 10 — Bass walks it off from 57 in the rain
paragraphs: Tyler Bass hit a 57-yard field goal as time expired to beat Kansas City 13-10 in Buffalo. It was a wet, windy, ugly night — rain all game, mid-30s, gusts near 30 mph — and the kicking game decided it.
The Bills are 10-1 now, alone at the top of the AFC. The Chiefs fall to 8-3. Emmett Johnson started again for Kansas City with Kenneth Walker III out, his third straight start.
The model had Buffalo by less than a point against a market of Buffalo -3. The market was right about the winner and wrong about the margin — and the total never had a chance in that weather.
items.takeaway: Buffalo stays on top of the AFC. The night game is done — Friday is about Denver and Pittsburgh now.

items.headline: Injury board: Watson still in protocol, and nothing new overnight
paragraphs: Christian Watson is still in the concussion protocol after the hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens on Wednesday night. He is uncertain for Week 13, but Green Bay does not play again until Sunday, Dec. 6, against New Orleans, so he has time to clear it.

No new overnight injury news moved a Sunday line. The games that matter today are the ones with inactives still to come — Denver at Pittsburgh names its inactives about 90 minutes before the 3:00 p.m. ET kickoff.
items.takeaway: Watson is a next-week question, not a today question. Watch the Friday inactives before kickoff.

items.headline: Rain in Pittsburgh again today for Broncos-Steelers
paragraphs: Denver at Pittsburgh kicks off at 3:00 p.m. ET at Acrisure Stadium, and it will be wet. Showers are expected, with a high of 41, a 70% chance of rain and wind around 15 mph.
That is the second straight wet, windy outdoor game after the rain in Buffalo last night. The total on the board is 36.5 on FanDuel and 37.5 on DraftKings, against a model total of 41.2.
items.takeaway: Another wet afternoon. Weather is a fact to know, not a totals edge on its own.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board held all three cards overnight
paragraphs: Hit Rate is still San Francisco moneyline -146 on FanDuel. The model gives the 49ers a 73.7% chance to beat Seattle. That is the job of Hit Rate: which supported pick looks most likely to win. It is not the plus-expected-value play, and it is not supposed to be. Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced is still New England moneyline -120 on FanDuel, with the model giving the Patriots a 58.3% chance against the Chargers. Value is still Indianapolis +6.5 at -115, the model's plus-expected-value play — and the edge ticked up overnight, from +0.7% to +1.6%.
Three cards, all Sunday games, all unchanged since last night. When the board holds, the old card is still the card. Bet the board as it stands.
items.takeaway: No swaps overnight. Same three Sunday cards, and the Value edge got a little better.

items.headline: No card on Broncos-Steelers today — use Check
paragraphs: The board has no card on Denver at Pittsburgh. The model is cooler than the market on the favorite: it has Denver by 1.8 against a market of Denver -4.5, and a model total of 41.2 against a market total near 37.

If your book has a number you like on this game, tap Check, type in the line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
Mason Rudolph starts for Pittsburgh. Bo Nix starts for Denver. Inactives land about 90 minutes before the 3:00 p.m. ET kickoff.
items.takeaway: No card is not a no. It means the board is quiet — Check your own number.

items.headline: Handle vs. tickets: two ways to count the same money
paragraphs: When you see betting splits, two numbers show up side by side: handle and tickets. Handle is the share of the money. Tickets is the share of the bets. They are not the same thing.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical. Say 70% of the tickets are on the favorite, but only 40% of the handle is. That means lots of small bets on the favorite and a few big bets on the other side. The crowd and the money disagree.

That disagreement is the start of a Fade conversation, not the end of one. One book's splits alone are not enough — you still want a second book or a line move pointing the same way before it means anything.
items.takeaway: Handle counts the money, tickets count the bets — when they point opposite ways, the crowd and the money disagree, and that is worth a second look, not a bet on its own.

items.headline: Cards unchanged overnight; the Value edge ticked up
paragraphs: Morning to evening to now, the three cards are the same three picks. Hit Rate is San Francisco moneyline -146 on FanDuel, Balanced is New England moneyline -120, Value is Indianapolis +6.5 at -115.

The Value card did move a little underneath: the edge went from +0.7% last night to +1.6% this morning, and the play-through moved from -116 to -118. The pick is the same. The price of the pick is nearly the same.
items.takeaway: A quiet overnight board. Same cards, slightly better Value edge.

items.headline: Same game, different number by book — New England and Indianapolis
paragraphs: New England is still -2.5 on DraftKings and -1.5 on FanDuel. That split has held since yesterday morning. The moneyline tells the same story: New England -137 on DraftKings, -120 on FanDuel.

Indianapolis is +6.5 on FanDuel and +6.0 on DraftKings. Denver -4.5 is unchanged everywhere. If your book is not DraftKings or FanDuel, your number may be different again — that is what Check is for. Type in your book's line and price and the app gives you a verdict on your number.
items.takeaway: The same game carries a different number depending on your book. Check your price, not somebody else's.

items.headline: Friday is a Check day — and the Sunday cards are already set
paragraphs: Broncos-Steelers kicks off at 3:00 p.m. ET in Pittsburgh, and the board has no card on it. If your book has a number you like, run it through Check before kickoff — and wait for inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff, if your bet depends on who is playing.

One timing note: the Sunday cards held overnight, and the Value edge got a little better. If your book has a good number on one of them now and Check says bet, bet now — a good number today beats a hoped-for number Sunday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
And a word on the tracker, since settlement is manual and there is no auto-settle: it only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Check your Friday number before kickoff, take a good Sunday number now if Check says bet, and log every result — losers included.

evidence.fact: Philadelphia beat Dallas 39-38 on Thursday, Nov 26, 2026, at AT&T Stadium. The Eagles trailed 28-10 at halftime and 31-10 in the third quarter, then outscored Dallas 22-7 in the fourth. Joe Milton, starting at quarterback for Philadelphia with Jalen Hurts out, threw for 331 yards and accounted for four touchdowns against his former team. Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left for the win, and Andrew Mukuba sealed it with a toe-tap interception. Dak Prescott threw for 265 yards and two touchdowns for Dallas; Javonte Williams had three total touchdowns. A Ty Robinson blocked punt and a big kickoff return swung the fourth quarter. Philadelphia improved to 4-7; Dallas fell to 5-7.
evidence.interpretation: A 21-point comeback decided at the gun — the third Thanksgiving game in a row decided in the final seconds. Dallas controlled most of the game and lost it late.

evidence.fact: Buffalo beat Kansas City 13-10 on Thursday, Nov 26, 2026, at Highmark Stadium, in the organization's first-ever home Thanksgiving game. Tyler Bass kicked a 57-yard field goal as time expired for the walkoff win. The game was played in heavy rain, mid-30s temperatures, and wind gusting near 30 mph. Buffalo improved to 10-1, the AFC's best record; Kansas City fell to 8-3. Rookie Emmett Johnson started at running back for Kansas City for a third straight game with Kenneth Walker III out.
evidence.interpretation: A field-position game in bad weather decided by the kicking game. Buffalo stays on top of the AFC; Kansas City's path to the top seed got harder.

evidence.fact: Green Bay WR Christian Watson is in the concussion protocol after the hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens late in the first half of Wednesday night's game against the Rams. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown before leaving, and the concussion was confirmed after he was evaluated in the locker room. Kinchens was ejected for the helmet-to-helmet hit. Watson is uncertain for Week 13; Green Bay does not play again until Sunday, Dec 6, against New Orleans, so he has extra time to clear protocol.
evidence.interpretation: Watson was Green Bay's leading receiver going into Wednesday night. His Week 13 status is a watch item for next week, not this one.

evidence.fact: Denver at Pittsburgh, Friday Nov 27, 2026, 3:00 p.m. ET kickoff at Acrisure Stadium (open air): showers expected, high 41 degrees, rain chance 70%, wind southwest around 15 mph. Overnight rain is expected Thursday into Friday, with rain or snow possible late Friday night.
evidence.interpretation: A wet, cold, windy afternoon in Pittsburgh. Weather is a fact to know, not a totals edge on its own.
